name: Membrane lamination
summary: A thin membrane with pores that block water drops. Pass water vapour, bonded between a face cloth and a liner to make a shell cloth.
how: Stretch the membrane of PTFE until it holds billions of pores in each square centimetre.
Bond the membrane between a nylon face cloth and a liner.
Tape each seam of the finished garment, so that no water enters at a stitch.

origin.note: W. L. Gore and Associates sells the first garment cloth with a stretched PTFE membrane.

adoptions.via: Gore-Tex shells give climbers a jacket that keeps out rain and lets out sweat.
Techwear labels build black city shells from membrane laminates with taped seams.
Gorpcore wears the bright membrane shell of the trail in the city.
